clinician.final_diagnosis: fatal invasive osteomyelitis in an allo-HSCT recipient caused by RM
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 73-year-old male with myelodysplastic syndrome RAEB I post-allogeneic stem cell transplantation presented with critical sepsis, fever, and respiratory failure requiring ventilation. Initial microbiology was negative despite bilateral infiltrates on CT. After initial respiratory recovery, the patient developed right hip pain and clinical deterioration. Imaging (MRI, CT, ultrasound) demonstrated multiple bone infarcts and massive secondary osteomyelitis with soft tissue extension in the right femur. Emergency proximal femoral resection revealed extensive bone and soft tissue destruction with blackened tissue. Bacterial cultures were negative after surgery, and a whole-body MRI 6 weeks later showed multiple further bone infarcts with suspected RM superinfection. Despite comprehensive investigation, no bacterial pathogens were identified, and clinical and imaging findings strongly suggested rare mold infection causing invasive osteomyelitis leading to fatal outcome.
